newsitem.title: USA: PGA - TORRANCE DUMPS NEW YEAR'S EVE FOR SHOT AT $ 1 MILLION.
newsitem.headline: PGA - TORRANCE DUMPS NEW YEAR'S EVE FOR SHOT AT $ 1 MILLION.

text.p: Sam Torrance made what for him was a huge sacrifice to prepare for the Andersen Consulting World Championship of golf.
"It's the first time in 43 years I've spent New Year's away from my own home, but a million dollars will do that to you," Torrance said.
"I've been known to celebrate New Year's quite strongly. I came over last Friday and I'm glad I did. I've enjoyed it here and the course is fabulous."
Torrance plays Scott Hoch Saturday in one semi-final at the Grayhawk course. Greg Norman meets Hisayuki Sasaki in the other semifinal.
The two winners advance to Sunday's 36-hole final, where the victor will collect $1 million from a total purse of $3.65 million, the richest in golf.

The $1 million first prize was enough to get Torrance's attention. He has played the course each day since his arrival, and on Thursday enjoyed a round with Phil Mickelson, a four- time winner on the PGA Tour last year.
Mickelson represents Grayhawk, and what he doesn't know about the course isn't worth knowing, but if Torrance learned anything from the American, he isn't saying.
"The subtleties I learned from Mickelson I ain't telling you," he said.
The matchplay event, in its second year, started with 32 players divided into four regional brackets.
Scotland's Torrance qualified for the semi-finals by winning the European section in May, while Hoch topped the American bracket in April.
Australian Norman won the "International" bracket in July, while Sasaki headed the Japanese section in March.
While Torrance, a veteran of eight Ryder Cups, and the consistent Hoch are probably even money bets for their semi- final, Norman is hot favourite to beat Sasaki.
Norman is interrupting a three-month break to play here, and after this weekend he will not play again until the Doral Open in Miami starting March 6.
"This is bad timing for me (but when I entered) I didn't know I was going to take three months off," said the world's top-ranked player.

"I haven't played in the desert that often. I haven't been in Phoenix for quite a few years. It's an excellent course for a matchplay championship because you can be a little aggressive. The fairways are fairly generous. It's the right venue for the right event.
"I'm fairly sharp. My only concern is my concentration over the entire round."
